draft.title: The powers of Augustus
card: Augustus avoided the title of king, which Romans hated. He called himself princeps, meaning first citizen, and said he had restored the Republic.
the powers of a tribune, such as the right to propose laws and to veto. Augustus held it from 23 BC and it gave him a legal basis to act for the people.
he controlled the provinces where most legions were stationed, and the soldiers swore loyalty to him. This gave him real military strength.
Together, these powers let Augustus hold control in practice while the old offices and the Senate still existed.
draft.remember: Augustus ruled through legal powers and the army, but called himself princeps, not king.

a.q: Why did Augustus call himself princeps rather than king?
opts: Romans hated kings, and princeps suited the Republic
Princeps gave him more legal power than king would
The Senate had banned him from using any other title
Princeps meant he was commander of all the legions
a.why: Romans distrusted the idea of a king, so Augustus took a modest title that fitted the Republic. Princeps did not give extra legal power. It only meant first citizen, so the option claiming more power is wrong.
a.clue: Think about how Romans felt about kings.

b.q: A historian argues that Augustus's real power rested on something other than his titles. Which evidence from his rule best supports this?
opts: Soldiers swore loyalty to him and he held the provinces
He took the title princeps, meaning first citizen
He kept the Senate and the old offices in place
He held tribunician power, which let him propose laws
b.why: Control of the provinces and the loyalty of the soldiers gave him real force, whatever his titles said. Princeps and the Senate's survival kept up the look of the Republic, and tribunician power was a legal basis, so these show titles and form rather than force.
b.clue: Which option is about force, not titles or legal form?

a.best: Romans hated kings, and princeps suited the Republic

b.best: Soldiers swore loyalty to him and he held the provinces
also_right: He held tribunician power, which let him propose laws
